about: Synthetic team meeting for evaluating whether summaries reflect the whole meeting (#162). Every name, product, system, and number is invented. It has no title and no stated purpose. It plants, each in its own stretch: a side issue that opens the meeting (staging certificate, 0:00), a control specific in a topic that never comes back (Parley seats, 2:00 to 3:55), a topic visited twice with different specifics each time (Quarry imports, 5:00 and 14:30), small talk with a greeting to leave out and a personal detail for Personal notes (7:00), the main topic with the most discussion (Bramble, 8:30 to 12:25), an idea suggested and not agreed (a daily digest, 9:43), a ticket discussed by number (WEB-1194, 13:30), and a line in the notes the meeting never discusses (hiring plan). Each expect entry lists accepted spellings separated by |.
notes:
- staging cert
- Parley renewal
- Quarry import timeouts
- Bramble rollout Monday
- ask about hiring plan for Q1
segments: Hi everyone, happy Thursday. Before anything else, quick one.
The TLS certificate on the staging load balancer expires this Saturday. Who can renew it?
Tomas here. I can do it. Is it still the wildcard certificate from the old vendor?
Yes, same one. The renewal email went to the shared ops inbox.
Okay, I'll renew it this afternoon and swap it on staging before Friday evening.
Thanks. If it lapses, the mobile test builds stop connecting, so let's not cut it close.
Next, the Parley analytics licenses. The renewal invoice came in.
Ilse here. We're paying for thirty-five seats, and the invoice is six thousand three hundred dollars for the year.
But only twenty-two people logged in during the last ninety days.
So we could drop seats. What's the minimum they'll sell?
Their minimum is twenty-five seats. At that size it comes to four thousand five hundred.
Tomas. Careful, the support team said they want three more seats in January for the new hires.
Then twenty-five leaves them no room. What about twenty-eight?
Ilse. Twenty-eight is five thousand and forty. Still more than a thousand cheaper than now.
Let's go with twenty-eight seats. Ilse, can you tell their account manager before the renewal date?
The renewal date is the third of November. I'll email them tomorrow.
One thing to know, unused seats don't roll over, so if we need more later we pay the full per-seat price mid-year.
That's fine. We can live with that risk for three people.
Also the Parley dashboards for the board deck need to move off the shared login before then, or they break when seats drop.
Good catch. Ilse, add that to the email to the account manager so they can move them.
Okay, Quarry imports. Fen, you were looking at the timeouts?
Fen here. Yes. Any import over fifty thousand rows times out. The job gives up after ninety seconds.
Smaller files are fine. A twenty thousand row file finishes in about forty seconds.
Is the ninety-second limit ours or the database's?
Ours. It's the job runner's default, nobody ever changed it.
We could, but then a stuck import holds a worker for longer. I'd rather find out why it's slow first.
Fair. Keep digging and we'll come back to it at the end if you have more.
Sure, I'm running a test import right now.
Wren here, sorry I'm late. Hi all.
Hey Wren, no problem. How was the trip?
Good, thanks. Oh, and heads up, I'm out from the twentieth of November for two weeks. My sister is getting married in Porto.
Wren. Thanks. I'll be fully offline, so whoever covers notifications will need the runbook.
Noted. Okay, we're all here, so let's get into it.
Bramble. Wren, where are we with the new notification service?
Wren. The Bramble service is done and running in staging. The plan is to switch ten percent of users over on Monday.
In staging the push delivery rate is ninety-seven point two percent. The old system sits around ninety-one.
Mostly devices that haven't opened the app in months, so their push tokens are stale. Bramble drops a token after three failed sends.
Tomas. And the old system never dropped them, which is why its rate is worse.
How do we roll back if something goes wrong on Monday?
Wren. There's a flag per user cohort. Setting it to zero sends everyone back to the old system within a minute. We tested that twice.
Bramble batches the digest emails every hour. Each person gets at most one email per hour, with everything since the last one.
Tomas. Honestly, I'd send the digest once a day instead of hourly. Hourly still feels like a lot of email.
Wren. Maybe. But support said people complained that daily was too slow when they're waiting on a reply.
Wren. I'd want to check with support before changing it. Let's not decide that today.
Okay, so hourly for now, and the daily idea stays open until Wren hears from support.
Fen. What about quiet hours? Do people get pushes at night?
Wren. Bramble respects the device's do not disturb, but it has no quiet hours of its own yet. That's an open question for product.
Which teams send the most notifications?
Wren. Orders sends about sixty percent of all pushes, then chat with about twenty-five. Orders is in the first ten percent on Monday.
Ilse. Is there a risk around the Apple push certificate? Ours expires in January.
Wren. Bramble uses the token-based key instead of the certificate, so the January expiry doesn't affect it. The old system still needs it renewed though.
Then let's not renew it unless the rollout slips past January.
Tomas. If we don't renew it and Bramble has a problem in January, we can't roll back.
Fair point. Renew it anyway, it's cheap insurance.
Wren. Okay, I'll renew it next week.
What's the plan after the first ten percent?
Wren. If the error rate stays under half a percent for a week, we go to fifty percent on the third of November, then everyone the week after.
Wren. If the error rate goes over half a percent, we roll back and look at it before trying again.
Who watches the dashboards on Monday?
Fen. I'm on call Monday, so I'll watch them. I'll post the numbers in the rollout channel at noon and at five.
And the runbook for while Wren is away?
Wren. I'll write it this week. It covers the cohort flag, the rollback, and where the delivery logs are.
Wren. One more. The unsubscribe link in digest emails is broken in staging. It points at the old preferences page. I'll fix it before Monday.
Good, that one would have hurt.
Ilse. That's the date picker bug. For users with a German locale, the calendar starts the week on Sunday instead of Monday.
Ilse. The fix reads the first day of the week from the locale instead of hard-coding it. It's in review.
Tomas. Me, I'll review it tomorrow morning.
Fen, back to Quarry. Did the test import finish?
Fen. Yes, and I found it. The import writes rows in batches of five hundred, so a fifty thousand row file makes a hundred round trips to the database.
Fen. I raised the batch size to two thousand in the test, and the same file finished in thirty-one seconds instead of timing out.
So we don't need to touch the ninety-second limit at all.
Fen. Right, the limit stays at ninety. I'd rather not hide slow imports behind a longer timeout.
Tomas. Any memory concern with bigger batches?
Fen. Memory went from about two hundred megabytes to three hundred during the import. That's well within the worker's limit.
Ship it then. Fen, can you open the change today?
Fen. Yes, today, and I'll run it against the largest customer file in staging first.
